recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12854 unless a future review identifies another active iCalendar mapping that reintroduces real personal contact details.
issue_request: FHIR-12854 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for DSTU2 asking that Appointment's iCalendar example mappings stop using Brian Postlethwaite's real name and email address and instead use fictitious example data such as John Doe.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git commit 6b63f8c4ffa9824ed42ddcfae87c94e39a78c2d9, "GF#12854: iCal mapping data anonymized", which changed the old Appointment spreadsheet mapping from ATTENDEE;CN="Brian Postlethwaite";...mailto:BPostlethwaite@data.com to ATTENDEE;CN="John Doe";...mailto:john@doe.com. Later source rework moved Appointment into source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml while retaining the fictitious mapping.
additional_context: Appointment remains an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current iCalendar mapping identity and Appointment.participant.status mapping in source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml use the fictitious John Doe/john@doe.com example, while searches for the original Postlethwaite name/email in current Appointment source found no remaining occurrence. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting discussion or minutes for FHIR-12854.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The authoritative current Appointment source already reflects the published Jira decision, and changing unrelated example narrative that merely uses the common first name Brian would exceed the issue scope because the Jira request concerned iCalendar mapping name/email content.
